title: Unit locus of the product-chart homogeneous coefficient
statement: Let $A=\bigoplus_{j\geq0}A_j$ be a nonnegatively graded commutative ring, $P=\operatorname{Proj}(A)$ [def-pc-proj], and $d,n\geq1$. Let $\alpha,\beta\geq0$ satisfy $\alpha=\beta+d$, and let $a\in A_\alpha$, $b\in A_\beta$, $f\in A_{nd}$ be homogeneous. Set $h=ab$, $k=\alpha+\beta>0$, $V=D_+(h)=\operatorname{Spec}R_0$, where $R=A_h$ is the graded localization and $R_0$ its degree-zero part [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero]. In $R$, the elements $a,b$ are units, the element $c=b^nf/a^n$ belongs to $R_0$, and $u=b^{2n\alpha}/a^{2n\beta}$ is a unit of $R_0$ with inverse $a^{2n\beta}/b^{2n\alpha}$. In $R_0$ one has $c^k=u f^k/h^{nd}$. For every $x\in V$, the germ $c_x\in\mathcal O_{V,x}$ is a unit if and only if $(f^k/h^{nd})_x$ is a unit, and these equivalent conditions hold if and only if $x\in D_+(f)$. Thus the principal open $D_V(c)=\{x\in V:c_x\text{ is a unit}\}$ equals $V\cap D_+(f)$, including when $V$ is empty or $f$ is zero or nilpotent.

source.place: Tag 01MV (lemma-principal-open), last two sentences of proof, coefficient principal open; Tag 01MA (lemma-standard-open-proj), affine-chart interpretation of D_+(h) intersect D_+(f).

proof.text: In the ordinary localization $R=A_h$, the defining inverse $h^{-1}$ gives $a^{-1}=b/h$ and $b^{-1}=a/h$, since $a(b/h)=b(a/h)=1$. Thus $c=b^{2n}f/h^n$. Its numerator has degree $2n\beta+nd=n(\alpha+\beta)=nk$, equal to the degree of $h^n$, so $c\in R_0$ by [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero]. Similarly $u=b^{2nk}/h^{2n\beta}$ and the proposed inverse $w=a^{2nk}/h^{2n\alpha}$ have numerator and denominator degrees respectively $2nk\beta$ and $2nk\alpha$, hence belong to $R_0$. Their product is $a^{2nk}b^{2nk}/h^{2n(\alpha+\beta)}=1$. This includes $\beta=0$, when the first denominator is $h^0=1$.

source.place: Tag 01MV (lemma-principal-open), coefficient b^n f/a^n on D_+(ab); explicit elementary fraction calculation supplying the last sentence.

proof.text: Put $v=f^k/h^{nd}$. Numerator and denominator both have degree $ndk$, so $v\in R_0$ by [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero]. Since $d=\alpha-\beta$ and $k=\alpha+\beta$, the exponents satisfy $2n\alpha-nd=nk$ and $2n\beta+nd=nk$. Using only the units $a,b$ already constructed, compute in $R$: $$uv=\frac{b^{2n\alpha}f^k}{a^{2n\beta}(ab)^{nd}}=\frac{b^{nk}f^k}{a^{nk}}=(b^nf/a^n)^k=c^k.$$ All terms lie in the subring $R_0$, so this is the asserted equality there; no cancellation of a nonunit or nonzero-divisor is used.

source.place: Tag 01MV (lemma-principal-open), coefficient b^n f/a^n on D_+(ab); explicit elementary fraction calculation supplying the last sentence.

proof.text: For $x\in V$, apply the germ ring map to $c^k=uv$ and $uw=1$. Then $c_x^k=u_xv_x$ and $u_xw_x=1$. If $c_x$ has inverse $t$, then $v_x=w_xc_x^k$ has inverse $u_xt^k$. Conversely, if $v_x$ has inverse $z$, then $c_x^{k-1}w_xz$ is an inverse of $c_x$, since $k\geq1$ and $c_x^kw_xz=u_xv_xw_xz=1$. Commutativity gives the other inverse identities as well. These explicit formulas prove both implications without any additional local-ring criterion.

source.place: Tag 01MV (lemma-principal-open), coefficient b^n f/a^n on D_+(ab); explicit elementary fraction calculation supplying the last sentence.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proj-basic-open-intersection] to its first homogeneous element $h=ab\in A_k$ and its second element $f\in A_{nd}$. Its positive-degree hypotheses hold: $k=2\beta+d>0$ and $nd>0$. Its chart is exactly $V=\operatorname{Spec}R_0$, and its function is $f^k/h^{nd}=v$. The cited germ-unit characterization therefore gives $v_x$ a unit if and only if $x\in V\cap D_+(f)$. Together with the preceding step this proves the desired pointwise equivalences and $D_V(c)=V\cap D_+(f)$.

source.place: Tag 01MV (lemma-principal-open), coefficient b^n f/a^n on D_+(ab); explicit elementary fraction calculation supplying the last sentence.

proof.text: If $V$ is empty, the pointwise claims and the equality of opens are vacuous, while all displayed ring identities still hold in the zero localization. If $f$ is zero or nilpotent, every prime ideal contains $f$ (if $f^N=0$, repeated primality gives $f\in\mathfrak p$). Thus $D_+(f)=\varnothing$ by [def-pc-proj]. Also $c$ is nilpotent by its formula $b^{2n}f/h^n$; in any stalk at a point a nilpotent unit would give $1=0$, impossible for the nonzero local ring at a point of a scheme. Equivalently, the preceding pointwise equivalence already shows its unit locus is empty.

source.place: Tag 01MV (lemma-principal-open), coefficient b^n f/a^n on D_+(ab); explicit elementary fraction calculation supplying the last sentence.

lean.statement: theorem productChartCoefficientLocus {A : Type u} {σ : Type v} [CommRing A] [SetLike σ A] [AddSubgroupClass σ A] (𝒜 : ℕ → σ) [GradedRing 𝒜] (d n α β : ℕ) (hd : 0 < d) (hn : 0 < n) (hα : α = β + d) (a b f : A) (ha : a ∈ 𝒜 α) (hb : b ∈ 𝒜 β) (hf : f ∈ 𝒜 (n * d)) : 0 < α + β ∧ IsUnit (algebraMap A (Localization.Away (a * b)) a) ∧ IsUnit (algebraMap A (Localization.Away (a * b)) b) ∧ ∃ c u w : HomogeneousLocalization.Away 𝒜 (a * b), c.val = algebraMap A (Localization.Away (a * b)) b ^ n * algebraMap A (Localization.Away (a * b)) f * Ring.inverse (algebraMap A (Localization.Away (a * b)) a) ^ n ∧ u.val = algebraMap A (Localization.Away (a * b)) b ^ (2 * n * α) * Ring.inverse (algebraMap A (Localization.Away (a * b)) a) ^ (2 * n * β) ∧ w.val = algebraMap A (Localization.Away (a * b)) a ^ (2 * n * β) * Ring.inverse (algebraMap A (Localization.Away (a * b)) b) ^ (2 * n * α) ∧ IsUnit u ∧ u * w = 1 ∧ c ^ (α + β) = u * HomogeneousLocalization.Away.isLocalizationElem (SetLike.mul_mem_graded ha hb) hf ∧ (∀ x : basicOpen 𝒜 (a * b), (IsUnit ((Proj 𝒜).presheaf.germ (basicOpen 𝒜 (a * b)) x x.2 (awayToSection 𝒜 (a * b) c)) ↔ IsUnit ((Proj 𝒜).presheaf.germ (basicOpen 𝒜 (a * b)) x x.2 (awayToSection 𝒜 (a * b) (HomogeneousLocalization.Away.isLocalizationElem (SetLike.mul_mem_graded ha hb) hf)))) ∧ (IsUnit ((Proj 𝒜).presheaf.germ (basicOpen 𝒜 (a * b)) x x.2 (awayToSection 𝒜 (a * b) c)) ↔ (x : Proj 𝒜) ∈ basicOpen 𝒜 f)) ∧ (Proj 𝒜).basicOpen (awayToSection 𝒜 (a * b) c) = basicOpen 𝒜 (a * b) ⊓ basicOpen 𝒜 f
